verse: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
story: Isaiah imagines a day when Judah will sing in the land, and the song begins with a city that stands and a peace that holds.

The promise is for the person whose mind is fixed, propped up and leaning on one thing. God keeps that person in peace, and the Hebrew doubles the word to say peace upon peace, a wholeness with nothing missing. The reason is simple: he trusts in the LORD. The next verse names Him the eternal Rock. Peace here is not the absence of trouble, since the song sits among distress. It is what a mind has when it rests on something that cannot move.
When your thoughts scatter this morning, bring them back to the Rock, one trusting thought at a time.
